The commit SHA is recorded in the N1E batch approval. Corpus v1's prior freeze stands at commit 1e2f11ae3b187a08a758b81b85de85d43f210757, recorded in RB-M3-N1 §0.20.2.
description: The instruments half of ADR-0031 decision 2's N3-start corpus extension, asserted against `gatebraid/coverage-report@1`. Covers IN-02's blocked remainder (a check that failed to notice), IN-03 (checker self-reference), IN-04 (moved HEAD / mutable ref recorded as replayable) and IN-05 (partial validator coverage claiming completeness). IN-01 IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT and does not freeze here — see known_limitation. IN1-05 and IN1-06 CONTAIN REAL FORBIDDEN INSTANCES: IN-03's rule, stated in CORPUS-v1-PLAN.md §3 and repeated in its IN-04 note, is that the negative case uses a real instance and only the REPORT is sanitized. The runner reports these as a locus and, for the additionalProperties case, a multiplicity — never the field name and never the value — so the checker does not quote what it forbids into its record (spec §4, ADR-0028 §3). Every locus was MEASURED. Digests: synthetic except `target.sha256`, as in bytes-platform.

case_provenance: R3-D method, recorded because the difference is the point. Every case here was constructed by the N1E executor — which authored neither N2 nor N3 — from the ITEM'S WRITTEN DESCRIPTION in M3-PLAN.md §6, CORPUS-v1-PLAN.md §3 and DETERMINACY-REPORT.md §2, NOT from the N3 draft's candidate cases, which were not read until after these were measured. That is what supplies the not-authored-by-the-implementer property here, in place of an external contribution. The two constructions were then compared and BOTH were kept wherever they differed: BP1-03/BP1-04 (this executor) and BP1-08 (the N3 draft) are three distinct loci over the same two remainders, and neither construction found the other's; IN1-07 (this executor) and IN1-11 (the N3 draft) likewise; IN1-12 was reached only by the N3 draft. Cases marked `independently_constructed` were reached by this executor before N3's were read; those marked `n3_draft_contributed` were not, and are carried on the transcribe-then-re-measure method that worked for the seven externally contributed cases at N1D. The residual is named: these are NOT externally contributed, and no external party reviewed them.
known_limitation: THREE items, all measured. (1) DECLARED LOCUS COLLISION: IN1-06 and IN1-11 produce an IDENTICAL locus — same keyword, same instance path, same absolute_schema_path — because a mutable name and an abbreviated object name fail the SAME 40-hex pattern at the same place. No locus refinement separates two values failing one constraint, and spec §4 bars separating them by echoing the values into the record. This is the EC1-28/EC1-29 class exactly, and the disposition follows that precedent: BOTH cases are carried and the collision is DECLARED here rather than papered over by dropping one, which would trade real coverage for a cosmetic tidy. Under the runner's equality rule either fixture would satisfy the other's manifest entry; that is the residual, and it is bounded to this pair. (2) IN-01 DOES NOT FREEZE IN THIS CORPUS. Its assertion — interpreting a pipeline exit code — spans this coverage report AND the target's `invocation.shell_semantics`, and no single locus in one document expresses it. That is ADR-0031's FIRST reopening condition ('an item still inexpressible at its own freeze point ... returns to an approved corpus change before the phase advances'), and this correct-course IS that approved corpus change: it RE-ASSIGNS IN-01's freeze point to corpus v2 at P's start, which M3-PLAN.md §6 already names as the next freeze. The property is not left unenforced meanwhile — N2's layer B refuses at write time to emit a record whose shell semantics and exit-code interpretation disagree, and that is IN-01's INTERIM ENFORCEMENT HOME. ADR-0031 decision 4 is satisfied because the re-assignment happens through the route the ADR itself names, not around it. (3) A CROSS-DOCUMENT ASSERTION MODE WAS REFUSED for now: growing a new instrument mid-flight is the move ADR-0028 §4 exists to prevent.
